name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (21 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found by 21 Nov; Kanlaon emitting minor ash
state: Phivolcs kept Kanlaon in the Philippines at alert level 2 after an ash emission 600 metres above the crater on 14 Nov and further ash on 15 and 16 Nov, and bars aircraft from flying near the summit (GMA News). Smithsonian GVP lists ongoing eruptions at volcanoes such as Semeru, Sangay and Fuego with routine ash advisories. Searches on 21 Nov found no red aviation colour code near major air routes, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: No volcanic ash is disrupting major air routes. Local flight changes are possible near active volcanoes in Indonesia, the Philippines and Central America; check with your airline.

sources.title: GMA News — Kanlaon Volcano emits 600-meter ash plume

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
